title: Authors’ Foundation
eligibility_summary: Writers previously published (or under contract) with a commercial UK or Irish publisher, sole author/translator, on a non-contributory contract; fiction, non-fiction, poetry, or script projects. No nationality or age restriction. Hybrid/self-published, editors, and AI-generated works ineligible; cannot fund publication/production costs or student tuition fees. Applicants who previously received an Authors’ Foundation or K Blundell grant must wait four years.
summary: Rolling work-in-progress grants to help develop a fiction, non-fiction, poetry, or script project — e.g. research, travel, or general expenditure beyond a publisher’s advance. No deadlines; accepts submissions year-round via emailed form.
notes: Own page: ‘There are no deadlines for this fund as it accepts submissions on a rolling basis’ and it is open year-round → status=rolling. Available to some UK-based researchers via non-fiction/research WIP grants (funds ‘important research, travel’). Page also references Arthur Welton Foundation and ‘grants for residential stays’ as related WIP funds, but neither has its own captured page in this snapshot (mirror gap) → not labelled. Amount is a typical range, not a hard cap.

title: Authors’ Contingency Fund
eligibility_summary: Professional authors resident in the UK or British citizens — fiction writers, illustrators, literary translators, scriptwriters, poets, journalists and others — for whom author-related activities make up a substantial part of annual income (actively writing over the past 3 years). Not open to editors, copywriters, salaried journalists, early-career/non-professional authors, or for a specific writing project.
summary: Small short-term hardship grants for established professional authors in financial crisis (e.g. lost income, project falling through, illness, one-off emergency expenses). Open year-round on a rolling basis; grant values vary to meet immediate need.
notes:
In scope per decision D6 (docs/DECISIONS-2026-08-28.md). The pre-registered inclusion rule carries no research-purpose clause — it asks only whether the call is open and available to some UK-based researchers — so this row is in_scope=yes, status=rolling. The page states no deadline and 'open year-round'.

The first pass argued for exclusion on purpose grounds: it is a welfare/hardship relief fund rather than a research or project-funding call, and explicitly excludes funding 'a specific writing project or to buy time to write'. D6 rejected that argument — adding a research-purpose clause after seeing the row would narrow the ground truth to fit intuition, and society-of-authors is a validation funder, so it would move the generalisation denominator. Tagged ambiguous_eligibility because the tension is real and an agent may reasonably hesitate.

title: K Blundell Trust
eligibility_summary: British-by-birth authors currently resident in the UK, under 40 (on 1 March 2026), whose work aims to increase social awareness; must have a previous sole-author work published with a commercial UK publisher (different from the WIP). One WIP only; hybrid/self-published, editors, and AI-generated works ineligible. Cannot hold both K Blundell and Authors’ Foundation in the same calendar year; four-year wait after a prior award.
summary: Work-in-progress grants (fiction, non-fiction, poetry, script) for British authors under 40 resident in the UK, whose work increases social awareness. Currently closed; re-opens for applications in 2027.
notes: Own page: ‘The K Blundell Trust has now closed and will re-open for applications in 2027’ → forthcoming, next_open_date=2027 (bare year, uncertain). Restricted: British-by-birth, UK-resident, under-40 only. Available to some UK-based researchers via non-fiction WIP. Aligns with Leverhulme bare-year ‘next opens’ treatment (forthcoming). No exact open date given.

title: P D James Memorial Fund
amount_raw: The fund currently distributes £2,500 per annum to each recipient
eligibility_summary: Authors aged 60 or over, or completely incapacitated for work, in financial hardship; awards made at the discretion of the P.D. James Memorial Fund Committee, which weighs necessity and the merit of the applicant’s work (long SoA membership a recommendation). Two members may apply on behalf of another.
summary: Regular discretionary annual payments (£2,500 p.a.) to a small number of authors in financial hardship who are aged 60+ or incapacitated. Currently closed for applications; committee-discretion pension-style fund.
exclusion_reason: Closed for applications on the snapshot date with no stated future open date; and it is a discretionary hardship/pension-style fund (committee-selected, not an open research call) → fails the inclusion rule.
notes: Own page: ‘The P D James Memorial fund is currently closed for applications’ with no re-open date given. Committee-discretion welfare payments for authors 60+ or incapacitated — not a research/project funding opportunity for UK-based researchers. Distractor.

title: Society of Authors’ Access Fund
amount_raw: designed to award small grants (usually £150 or less)
eligibility_summary: All authors — anyone who creates work for publication, broadcast or performance and meets SoA membership criteria (membership not required); UK and Irish residents or British/Irish citizens. One grant per calendar year; preference to those not previously funded. Cannot be used for events where the author is speaking, course fees, retrospective/already-attended events, publication/promotion costs, London Book Fair, or book launches.
summary: Small grants (usually £150 or less) for travel, subsistence, childcare/carer support, or access needs to attend events, writing residencies, and retreats. Currently closed; expected to re-open for applications in 2027; normally assessed on a rolling basis.
notes: Own page: ‘The SoA Access Fund is closed for applications and is currently expected to re-open for applications in 2027’ → forthcoming, next_open_date=2027 (bare year, uncertain). Amount usually ≤£150 (applications for more accepted) → max recorded 150, min blank/uncertain. Available to some UK-based author-researchers (e.g. travel to attend research-relevant events/residencies). One-per-year and preference rules noted (restricted).

title: Strachey Trust Grants
eligibility_summary: All authors as defined by SoA Full Membership criteria (membership not required) who are UK resident or British citizens, working on a specific full-length literary project with a strong likelihood of publication, wishing to access UK/Republic of Ireland archives or collections. Excludes undergraduate, Masters, or PhD research; self-published/author-funded projects; permission fees; retrospective access. One application per calendar year; four-year wait after a successful award.
summary: Rolling grants up to £500 to enable authors to travel to a UK or Republic of Ireland archive/collection to research unpublished manuscript material for a specific full-length literary project likely to be published. Assessed on a rolling basis (usually within two weeks).
notes: Own page: ‘All claims are assessed on a rolling basis (usually within two weeks)’ and no deadline → status=rolling. Available to UK-based researchers (biographers, historians, researchers accessing manuscripts) — though academic UG/Masters/PhD research is explicitly excluded, so eligibility for a UK academic researcher is partial (project must be a publishable full-length literary book, not degree research). Application form is a downloadable document (pdf_only tag). Amount up to £500; min blank (no floor stated).
